Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.infrastructure.persistence.dev

Class DevDataInitializer

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.infrastructure.persistence.dev.DevDataInitializer
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner
@Component @Profile("dev") public class DevDataInitializer extends Object implements org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner
Seeds a demo user, a confidential BFF client and a public device-flow client when the dev profile is active, so a freshly started authorization server has someone to sign in, a client to sign in through and a client for the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (device-client, which the polling command line tool of the service-client uses).

The device-client is dev-only on purpose: it is a public client that anybody who can reach the server can use to start a device flow, and its user-facing name and scopes are those of a demo. A deployment registers its own device clients through the admin API with the urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code grant type.

Purpose: local development and the end-to-end tests. Started with spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=dev, it lets a developer sign in through the BFF by hand. The e2e-tests module (SignInSmokeIT) starts the packaged jar with the dev profile and reads the generated credentials from the log lines below.

Why it lives in src/main although it only seeds demo data: the end-to-end tests run the real jar, and a class under src/test never reaches it. It is inert everywhere else: without the dev profile the bean is not even created. Never activate that profile outside local development.

It lives in the persistence adapter, next to the Flyway migrations, because it writes the tables those migrations create: a schema change that breaks it is then caught by this module's own tests.

Secrets are generated at first start and logged once as DEV ONLY warnings; nothing is committed. Running it again does not change existing data.
